newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gle Eaux, SGE firm on outlooks.
newsitem.headline: Gle Eaux, SGE firm on outlooks.

text.p: Shares in Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) and its SGE unit strengthened on Tuesday, as the market welcomed steps to reorganise the construction subsidiary.
CGE chairman Jean-Marie Messier outlined on Monday plans to make SGE the centre for the group's electrical installations, roadbuilding, construction and heating activities.
"Messier's managed it very well," said one trader. "The market likes the way he is addressing the problems one by one and presents it all logically."
CGE was up 3.22 percent at 609 francs, while SGE firmed 7.99 percent to 96 at 0910 GMT.
Messier plans for SGE to return to a "significant level" of profit in 1997 and to make it "radically different and attractive."

Under restructuring plans, CGE will transfer its GTIE and Santerne units to Societe Generale d'Entreprises (SGE), to create with SGE's SDEL an electrical installations group with 11 billion francs of annual sales.
Roadbuilding firms Cochery, Viafrance and SGE-VBU will be brought into SGE, making a group with annual sales of 11 billion francs.
The construction arm will be reorganised with SGE buying 40 percent of the capital of Compagnie Generale de Batiment et de Construction (CBC) which is currently 100 percent owned by CGE.

Separately, a judge investigating nearly 13 million francs in suspicious billings paid by CGE in 1992-1994 formally placed under investigation on Monday Robert Hue, head of the French Communist Party, and predecessor Georges Marchais.
Some 70 primarily leftist towns were preparing to award water contracts in that period.
On the French island of Reunion, two senior CGE executives admitted in court last week the group had funded elected officials on the island from 1991.
